floors.cause: For questions the intent grammar cannot express, the stand-in model often answers a nearby question instead of refusing. Example: asked for a percentage, it returned a count per status. Each such answer is a wrong answer, not a refusal.
floors.next: v0.2 changes the prompt to refuse first when a question needs something the grammar lacks, then measures it on a fresh run. The v0.1 prompt is not changed after seeing these results.

misses.note: Ambiguous date: the answer filtered on completion date (when parts are used), the gold on opening date. Both readings are defensible.
Ambiguous date: 'did work for last month' was read as completed last month; the gold uses opened last month.
Needs the difference between two dates (opened to completed). Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: Average days to complete needs the elapsed time between work_orders.opened_at and work_orders.completed_at, and the registry has no way to compute a difference between two date fields. Metrics aggregate a single field only.

misses.note: Needs a ratio of two counts. The model returned counts per status instead of refusing: a wrong answer, not a refusal.
Needs a computed value (quantity times unit price). Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: Parts revenue needs quantity times unit_price per line, and the registry has no computed line-revenue field. A metric aggregates a single field, so summing unit_price or quantity alone would give a different number.

misses.note: Needs two date fields in one monthly series. The model counted completions among the orders opened each month instead of refusing: a wrong answer.
Needs a distinct count of months in HAVING. The model returned per-technician monthly counts instead of refusing: a wrong answer.
Needs date arithmetic and a ratio. Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: The question needs a 2-day elapsed-time test between completed_at and opened_at and a ratio of two counts; the intent language supports neither a date arithmetic comparison nor a share metric.

misses.note: Needs a conditional count beside a sum. Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: The question needs two different row sets at once: a sum over unpaid and overdue invoices, and a count of overdue invoices only per customer. Filters apply to every row and having applies to whole groups, so the registry cannot express a conditional count alongside the sum.

misses.note: Needs an anti-join (sites with no work orders). Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: Finding sites with no work orders in a window needs an anti-join (sites with no matching work_orders rows), which this intent format cannot express. Filters on work_orders fields only return sites that do have matching rows.
